assessment: P-02-10 concerns anti-PD-1 cancer immunotherapy and mortality in lung cancer.

Ishida P-04-8 analyzes 30 of 33 Parkinson PEG patients, with 15 eating orally before PEG, six after it, and two continuing four months or more. The median to death or tracheostomy is 32 months (95% CI 15–113). Findings and counts closely match the June 2023 Iou Hospital neurology presentation. There are no named meals or ingredient-specific outcomes.
P-13-2 defines PD as pancreaticoduodenectomy in a surgical study of sarcopenia.

P-01-5 reports low recorded glucose and weight loss in a Parkinson tube-feeding case. Weight recovered after energy increased, but occasional low readings persisted and normalized when samples were drawn immediately before feeding. The authors suspect variable 1–6-hour delays before specimen submission. Formula ingredients and a causal food result are absent.
P-03-1 concerns delayed gastric emptying after pancreaticoduodenectomy, which is what PD denotes.

P-15-7 reports a Parkinson patient with multiple injuries and suspected aspiration pneumonia. Sputum and oral hygiene improved after switching to an unnamed semisolid tube formula. Swallowing rehabilitation and a palatal prosthesis accompanied progression through texture codes 0j and 1j to code 2. No culinary ingredient or food-specific outcome is reported.
P-19-4 describes gastric leakage and skin problems in an 88-year-old Parkinson patient. Shortening the gastrostomy button shaft corrected the problem. The formula is unnamed.

P-19-5 describes an 88-year-old Parkinson patient with cerebral amyloid angiopathy and PEG. Less delayed gastric emptying, vomiting and aspiration pneumonia followed a fermented-ingredient formula change plus altered delivery rate and frequency. A September 2023 report describes the same patient and intervention. Culinary exposure and isolated component effects are unresolved.
P-21-1 counts 39 Parkinson diagnoses among 159 nutrition-team rounds on a mixed ward. Food order changes and outcomes are aggregate without a Parkinson-specific ingredient result.

P-27-9 uses indirect calorimetry in a Parkinson patient with postoperative ileostomy, watery effluent and weight loss. Tube-feed energy and protein were reported and delivery changes proposed. There are no named ingredients or measured outcomes after the proposed changes.

P-28-1 is the Utano 129-patient cross-sectional cough-sensitivity cohort also reported at 2023 JSDNNM O-09. Wet voice was associated with low cough sensitivity (OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.1–8.1). The test uses inhaled citric acid in saline and there is no dietary exposure.

P-28-2 reports 27 of 80 Parkinson cases with severe hypoglycemia and adds 12 of 98 in a comparison group with other diagnoses (p<.001). The Parkinson count and 637.6 versus 932.4 kcal/day match the 2023 NHO report. No individual foods were assessed.
